'''Black Rock''' is a neighborhood in the southwestern section of the city of [[Bridgeport, Connecticut]]. It borders [[Fairfield, Connecticut|Fairfield]] and the [[Ash Creek (Connecticut)|Ash Creek]] tidal estuary on the west, the West Side/West End of Bridgeport on the north and east, and [[Black Rock Harbor]] and [[Long Island Sound]] on the south. Black Rock comprises [[census tract]]s 701 and 702 and part of census tract 703.<ref name="blackrockonline1">{{cite web|url=http://www.blackrockonline.org/sites/blackrockonline.org/files/BR_NRZ_Plan_v8_0.pdf |title=Neighborhood Revitalization Zone Plan, Black Rock Neighborhood, Bridgeport, CT, Final Draft |date=March 8, 2008 |accessdate=2014-06-20}}</ref> It includes two [[historic district (United States)|historic district]]s listed on the [[National Register of Historic Places]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Black Rock Historic District|url=https://npgallery.nps.gov/NRHP/AssetDetail?assetID=ab1cd144-1f5e-4355-84d5-c3d6158584e8|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200710152718/https://npgallery.nps.gov/NRHP/AssetDetail?assetID=ab1cd144-1f5e-4355-84d5-c3d6158584e8|archive-date=2020-07-10|access-date=2020-07-10|website=npgallery.nps.gov|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Black Rock Gardens Historic District|url=https://npgallery.nps.gov/NRHP/AssetDetail?assetID=925a6cbf-7e43-439d-967d-99ebeaaf92e8|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200710153113/https://npgallery.nps.gov/NRHP/AssetDetail?assetID=925a6cbf-7e43-439d-967d-99ebeaaf92e8|archive-date=2020-07-10|access-date=2020-07-10|website=npgallery.nps.gov|language=en-US}}</ref> Residences comprise 86% of properties in Black Rock, 10% are commercial, and 4% are industrial or other property classes.<ref name="blackrockonline1" />

==History==
Black Rock was first settled in 1644 by a group of settlers led by [[Thomas Wheeler (soldier)|Thomas Wheeler]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=The First Settlers of Black Rock|url=https://bportlibrary.org/hc/neighborhood-black-rock/the-first-settlers-of-black-rock/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200710151624/https://bportlibrary.org/hc/neighborhood-black-rock/the-first-settlers-of-black-rock/|archive-date=2020-07-10|access-date=2020-07-10|website=Bridgeport History Center|language=en-US}}</ref> The region was also inhabited by [[Native Americans in the United States|Native Americans]], who relinquished their settlement in the area in 1681.<ref name=":2" />

[[Image:oldfairfieldmap.gif|thumb|alt=Early Map of Fairfield and Black Rock - Before the settlement of Bridgeport.| Early Map of Fairfield and Black Rock - Before the settlement of Bridgeport.]]

During the early days of Black Rock, the area was also the community of Stratfield, which has also been absorbed into modern [[Bridgeport, Connecticut|Bridgeport]].{{Citation needed|date=July 2020}}  Stratfield was originally known as Pequonnock and was located about midway between Black Rock and the original settlement of Bridgeport.{{Citation needed|date=July 2020}}  The cemetery known as Stratfield Burying Place is located here and has many of Black Rock's early settlers interred there.{{Citation needed|date=July 2020}}

In 1653, [[Goodwife Knapp]] was executed for witchcraft in a field in Fairfield; today, the field is located within the limits of Black Rock, with a community centre built on its site.<ref name=":62">{{Cite news |last=Schier |first=Anne |date=2019-08-15 |title=Fairfield Woman Hanged For Witchcraft To Be Honored With Memorial |url=https://patch.com/connecticut/fairfield/memorial-honor-fairfield-woman-hanged-witchcraft |access-date=2025-10-12 |work=Patch |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Dunavin |first=Davis |date=2021-10-21 |title=Beyond Salem: New England's other witch hunts were in Connecticut |url=https://www.wshu.org/podcast/off-the-path-from-new-york-to-boston/2021-10-21/beyond-salem-new-englands-other-witch-hunts-were-in-connecticut |access-date=2025-10-12 |work=WSHU Public Radio |language=en}}</ref>

Black Rock was incorporated into Bridgeport in 1870.<ref name=":2" />

In the late 19th century and early 20th century, wealthy merchants built homes in Black Rock in an array of different architectural styles, including [[Mediterranean Revival architecture|Mediterranean Revival]] and [[Tudor Revival architecture|Tudor Revival]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|last=Prevost|first=Lisa|date=2002-06-09|title=If You're Thinking of Living In/St. Mary's-by-the-Sea, Conn.; At Peninsula's End, a Waterside Enclave|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/06/09/realestate/if-you-re-thinking-living-st-mary-s-sea-conn-peninsula-s-end-waterside-enclave.html|url-status=live|access-date=2020-07-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200710155124/https://www.nytimes.com/2002/06/09/realestate/if-you-re-thinking-living-st-mary-s-sea-conn-peninsula-s-end-waterside-enclave.html|archive-date=2020-07-10|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> One of these homes, with {{convert|3|acre|m2}} of land and 16 rooms ("The Chimneys"), is located on Old Battery Road.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Prevost |first=Lisa |date=2008-03-09 |title=When Location Is the Enemy |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/03/09/realestate/09wczo.html |access-date=2023-02-10 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>
The S. S. Norden Club is a private club founded in 1902, the first of a number of private clubs in the neighborhood.{{Citation needed|date=July 2020}}

A [[Carnegie library|Carnegie Library]] was built in the neighborhood in 1932, which would later become the Black Rock Branch Library, a branch of the Bridgeport Public Library system.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=About The Black Rock Branch Library|url=https://bportlibrary.org/about-black-rock/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200710162315/https://bportlibrary.org/about-black-rock/|archive-date=2020-07-10|access-date=2020-07-10|website=Bridgeport Public Library|language=en-US}}</ref>

===Historic districts===
There are two [[historic district (United States)|historic districts]] in the neighborhood that have been listed on the [[National Register of Historic Places]].  The [[Black Rock Historic District]] was created on March 15, 1979, and comprises a number of houses and other structures from the mid 18th Century through the late 19th Century.<ref name=":0" />  The other historic district is the [[Black Rock Gardens Historic District]], created on September 26, 1990.<ref name=":1" />  The district comprises 7 acres of emergency housing built for workers during [[World War I]].<ref name=":1" />

=== Present-day ===
[[File:BridgeportCT BlackRockHD QueenAnneHouses.jpg|thumb|left|Queen Anne-style houses within the Black Rock Historic District]]Black Rock maintains a leafy and seaside character which is typically viewed in stark contrast to the more industrial and urban character of Bridgeport as a whole.<ref name=":5">{{Cite news|last=Hughes|first=C. J.|date=2010-05-21|title=St. Mary's-by-the-Sea, Conn.|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/05/23/realestate/23Living.html|url-status=live|access-date=2020-07-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200710153919/https://www.nytimes.com/2010/05/23/realestate/23Living.html|archive-date=2020-07-10|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Despite this, the area is more affordable compared to many of the surrounding towns, partially due to the association of the neighborhood with Bridgeport.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite news|last=Prevost|first=Lisa|date=2004-08-08|title=LIVING IN/Black Rock, Conn.; A Community With Spirit, and an Edge|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/08/08/realestate/living-in-black-rock-conn-a-community-with-spirit-and-an-edge.html|url-status=live|access-date=2020-07-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200710154541/https://www.nytimes.com/2004/08/08/realestate/living-in-black-rock-conn-a-community-with-spirit-and-an-edge.html|archive-date=2020-07-10|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

The neighborhood maintains a diverse character, with sizable [[Irish Americans|Irish]], [[Mexican Americans|Mexican]], [[Jamaican Americans|Jamaican]], and [[Indian Americans|Indian]] communities.<ref name=":6" /> Many who move to the neighborhood are retirees, but the area is also home to a small but growing art scene.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" />

In July 2009, the Black Rock Branch Library, the area's library, expanded in size from 6,000 to 11,000 square feet, and was renovated to be outfitted with [[Wi-Fi|wi-fi]] and public computers.<ref name=":4" />

On December 5, 2011, the [[Fairfield Metro station]] opened, which eased the burden on [[Fairfield station (Metro-North)|Fairfield station]], and made commuting via Metro-North easier for Black Rock residents.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Fairfield Metro Station|url=https://fairfieldct.org/fairfieldmetrostation|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200710161324/https://fairfieldct.org/fairfieldmetrostation|archive-date=2020-07-10|access-date=2020-07-10|website=fairfieldct.org|publisher=Town of Fairfield, Connecticut}}</ref>

While the neighborhood is overwhelmingly residential, there is a significant commercial presence along Fairfield Avenue, the main thoroughfare, which connects Black Rock to Fairfield and downtown Bridgeport.<ref name="blackrockonline1" /> Fairfield Avenue is in a state of transition with older businesses being replaced by upscale restaurants, cafes, espresso bars, gourmet ice cream shops, and art galleries.{{Citation needed|date=July 2020}}

The neighborhood's residential areas lie on either side of Fairfield Avenue, with the area of least density being a section called St. Mary's-by-the-Sea, which consists of Resident AA zoned properties (which require a minimum lot of 11,250 SF).<ref name="blackrockonline1" /> Grovers Hill is the highest elevation in Black Rock and some of the most expensive properties in Black Rock are located on this hill with views of Long Island Sound.{{Citation needed|date=July 2020}}  There are also direct waterfront properties, including two condominium complexes on the Sound and two on the Ash Creek tidal estuary.{{Citation needed|date=July 2020}}  St. Mary's-by-the-Sea also has a {{convert|9|acre|m2|adj=on}} public park along the Sound with half a mile of sidewalks and an area for bird watching.{{Citation needed|date=July 2020}}

==Transportation==
[[File:Fairfield Metro station under pedestrian bridge, May 2012.jpg|thumb|Black Rock is served by [[Fairfield-Black Rock station]] on the [[New Haven Line]]]]
[[Connecticut Route 130|Fairfield Avenue]] is Black Rock's primary artery. Black Rock is also accessible from exit 25 on [[Interstate 95 in Connecticut|I-95]] and from [[U.S. Route 1 in Connecticut|Route 1]], both of which run just north of the area. Black Rock is served by the [[Fairfield–Black Rock station]] on [[Metro-North Railroad|Metro-North's]] [[New Haven Line]], located just across [[Ash Creek (Connecticut)|Ash Creek]] in neighboring [[Fairfield, Connecticut|Fairfield]], which opened on December 5, 2011.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":7" />

Two [[Greater Bridgeport Transit]] bus routes run in Black Rock, primarily along Fairfield Avenue. The Coastal Link, a service provided in conjunction with the [[Norwalk Transit District]] and the [[Milford Transit District]], runs eastbound to the [[Connecticut Post Mall]] in Milford and westbound to the Norwalk Wheels Hub in [[Central Norwalk]]. Greater Bridgeport Transit's Route 5 runs south along Brewster Street (the primary north–south artery that links the neighborhood to neighboring Fairfield) and provides additional eastbound service along Fairfield Avenue. Route 5's primary terminus is the intermodal transit center in Downtown Bridgeport, where riders can make connections to several other bus routes and [[Bridgeport station (Connecticut)|Metro-North]]. Service along these routes typically run every 30 minutes Monday through Saturday, while Sunday service is hourly.

== Business Association ==
The Black Rock Business Association (BRBA), originated in 2005, is a group of Black Rock business owners who work together to promote Black Rock as a shopping, dining and entertainment district.

The Black Rock Business Association's activities include:
*Black Rock Harvest Hootenanny
*Managing local website and calendar for www.EnjoyBlackRock.com
*Seasonal neighborhood clean-up projects
*Business development workshops, open to the community
*Sponsorship of neighborhood enhancements, such as trash pick-up

== Climate ==
Black Rock has an overall moderate climate, the average January temperature is around 23 degrees (F) and the average high in July is 82 degrees (F).<ref>US Climate data</ref> Black Rock has in the past been hit with a number of large winter snow storms. Although the average snowfall is 29", the following is the list of top snow-accumulating winters (October 1 - April 30):<ref>National Weather Service</ref>
# 1995-96 - 75.7"
# 2002-03 - 64"
# 2010-11 - 62.6"
# 1966-67 - 61.6"
# 2012-13 - 61.3"
